newsitem.title: USA: U.S MUNICIPAL FOCUS - Market unmoved, FOMC ahead.
newsitem.headline: U.S MUNICIPAL FOCUS - Market unmoved, FOMC ahead.

text.p: U.S. Municipal bond prices opened unchanged Monday as Tuesday's FOMC meeting stifled action.
"The market is kind of on hold," one trader said, citing the Fed meeting. "It's a Monday morning, a very light new issuance week."
The FOMC meeting is widely expected to bring a 25-basis-point tightening in short-term rates.

"I think everyone expects them to tighten a little, I think that's kind of in the market," a second trader said, adding that he saw this week's Treasury market auction of two-year and five-year notes as having a greater impact.
"The two-year and five-year auctions are more important at this point than what the Fed does tomorrow," the trader said.
The government is scheduled to sell $17.25 billion of two-year notes on Tuesday and $12.5 billion of five-year notes on Wednesday.

In the government market, the benchmark 30-year bond was up 5/32 at 95-28/32 to yield 6.95 percent. In debt futures, the June municipal contract was up 1/32 at 113-8/32. The June T-bond contract was up at 2/32 at 108-25/32. The MOB spread was 143 ticks.
As for new issues, deals are expect to total $1.9 billion this week, down sharply from roughly $3.7 billion last week.
This week's negotiated offerings are expected to total $1.5 billion in 40 sales, with a $600 million Hawaii general obligation deal through Smith Barney Inc. topping the the list.
On the competitive side, 44 sales totaling $347 million are scheduled, with a $45 million Oakland, Calif., deal on Wednesday the largest.
